outer_exit143.supported_mechanism: The coordinator records a marker-bearing bash command and Python subprocess.run awaiting wrapper rather than exec replacement. Independently reopened track_processes() excludes only its own PID and admits current process-group members, descendants of recorded PID/start identities, or commands containing CYCLE_MARKER. This can select marker-bearing awaiting ancestors.
outer_exit143.signaling_guard: stop_owned_workers() waits five seconds, rechecks PID/start/command identity before SIGTERM/SIGKILL, and records PID/start/signal but not the selected command.
outer_exit143.inference_limit: No retained pre-signal PID-to-command mapping proves that these exact two PIDs were bash/Python. Matching start times corroborate the mechanism but are not proof. The inner receipt's generic unrelated-process exclusion sentence is not independent evidence of exact selected process identities.
outer_exit143.distinction: The four focused commands and Gradle stop each returned zero, while the enclosing tool session actually returned 143. Scoped test/mechanism results are supportable; calling the whole invocation PASS is not.
outer_exit143.future_invocation_correction: Use exec replacement of the launcher by the unchanged archived runner, without cycle-marker-bearing waiting ancestors. No archived runner edit or repeat of this already completed batch is requested.
